summary: Built the §3 sea. Map: Tiled source assets/source/maps/slice-sea.tmj (documented subset in packages/content/src/tiledMap.ts) converted by scripts/build-map.ts (npm run map:build / map:check, via tsx) into packages/content/src/maps/sliceSea.ts; validateSeaMap checks four small islands with docks, shoals, eight outer-sea spawn slots pairwise beyond ENGAGEMENT_RANGE_TILES (6), reachability, nearest-island 20-40 s (actual 22-23 s), longest crossing <= 90 s (54 s) and first dock <= 40 s; a unit drift test (Vite ?raw import, content tsconfig unchanged) fails when the module is out of date. Simulation: 64-heading literal cosine table, throttle/brake/slow reverse/drag/turn, swept axis-separated hull collision (slides, runs aground, no tunnelling at any speed), docking with E at low speed near a dock (records dock id, throttle casts off), placeShip, visibleShipIds; state stays integer. Server: ships map tagged .view(), per-client StateView updated after every mirror, public players count, protocol v3, test-only POST /__test/place served only when the dev/test entry (apps/server/src/dev.ts) reads PIRATE_SEA_RACE_TEST_PLACEMENT=1. Web: keyboard helm with E, Phaser tilemap (sea cells left empty for software-renderer speed), camera follow, sight circle, only-visible ships listed and drawn, HUD dock state, minimap with client-side fog. Docs: architecture.md and README updated. Checks I ran: npm run typecheck (pass), npm run test:unit (131 passed), npm run test:integration (21 passed, incl. visibility on decoded state and raw frames), npm run build (pass, smoke also checks the production entry has no placement route), Playwright all four scenarios passed three times; the JSON-report run passed workflow check-report (4 ok).
open_assumptions: The .tmj was laid out with a throwaway script (not in the repo) and never opened in the Tiled editor (not installed); it follows Tiled 1.10+ JSON conventions with an image-less tileset because art is placeholder-only.

Travel targets are read as: each island's nearest other island by sea, dock to dock, 20-40 s; longest useful crossing = longest shortest path between any two docks or spawn slots; §2's first useful stop checked as nearest dock <= 40 s with no lower bound.
'Outer sea' means outside the bounding box of the island rectangles; spawn slots are checked pairwise (stronger than adjacent-only) against ENGAGEMENT_RANGE_TILES = 6; SIGHT_RADIUS_TILES = 10.
Input message fields keep their names (moveX turns, moveY is the throttle, negative ahead); their meaning changed, so PROTOCOL_VERSION is now 3.
Dock labels use the four cardinal sides of the island rectangle (e.g. 'Palm Key, south dock').

Browser tests place ships through the test-only route and steer with a closed-loop keyboard autopilot reading the HUD's authoritative readout; sea scenarios have a 120 s timeout for a loaded verifier.
